title: LeanStream: A Speculate-and-Refine Streaming Framework for Efficient on-Device LLM Inference
authors: Renyuan Liu, Yuyang Leng, Kaiyan Liu, Yuzhou Zhong, Shaohan Hu, Chun-Fu (Richard) Chen, Peijun Zhao, Heechul Yun, Shuochao Yao
abstract: On-device LLM inference is attractive for privacy and responsiveness, but remains challenging on mobile and embedded devices because model weights far exceed available DRAM. Prior systems exploit sparse activations and offload parameters to SSDs, but encounter a core tension: precise sparse selections need current context, while overlapping compute and I/O demands early guessing. LeanStream is a streaming speculate-and-refine framework that continuously adjusts processing, fetching, and cache-keeping priorities via incomplete GPU outputs, allowing detailed interleaving of GPU compute and storage transfers. Tested on smartphones and embedded boards, LeanStream reduces memory usage by 4.8x to 7.5x while improving token generation throughput by 1.6x to 2.1x compared to prior on-device baselines.

title: AceSpec: An Asymmetric Edge-Cloud Collaborative Framework for Communication-Efficient LLM Inference
authors: Yida Zhang, Zhiyong Gao, Shuaibing Yue, Jie Li, Rui Wang
abstract: Deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) on edge devices typically relies on model compression or split inference. However, compression degrades reasoning capabilities, while split inference suffers from severe latency over bandwidth-limited networks. Speculative decoding offers a promising alternative where a smaller edge unit generates draft tokens for remote verification, but unstable connections cause unavoidable rejections that halt operations. AceSpec introduces an asymmetric edge-cloud collaborative framework that uses idle edge compute to proactively construct a probabilistic state cache, converting massive system resets into rapid local memory lookups. The system uses a unique transfer protocol sending compact primary-chain markers upward and brief scattered probabilities downward. A connection-conscious optimization approach continuously boosts onboard reserve success frequency. Tests show 3.52x throughput speedup even under severely constrained 50 Kbps WAN conditions.
edge_agent_evidence: 端云协同LLM推理框架，50Kbps下3.52x吞吐提升
recommendation_reason: 直接解决低带宽条件下的端侧LLM推理问题

title: Diffusion Language Models for Mobile Edge Agentic AI: Foundations, Applications, and Challenges
authors: Chenqi Li, Minghui Min, Dusit Niyato, Wei Ni
abstract: This survey examines diffusion language models (DLMs), which provide a non-autoregressive alternative for mobile edge agentic artificial intelligence by refining tokens through iterative denoising rather than left-to-right generation. DLMs can update multiple uncertain tokens in parallel and exploit bidirectional context, offering advantages for edge computing scenarios. The paper analyzes DLM suitability for resource-constrained environments, addressing latency, memory, energy, bandwidth, privacy, and reliability constraints. Coverage includes efficient architectures, acceleration techniques, compression methods, and deployment strategies across edge and cloud infrastructure. Applications discussed span IoT and wireless systems, with the survey also examining challenges like long-context state management, split inference, trustworthy execution, multimodal grounding, and reproducible benchmarking.

title: Atlas: Algorithm-Hardware Co-Design for On-Device City-Scale 3D Gaussian Splatting in VR
authors: He Zhu, Zheng Liu, Xingyang Li, Anbang Wu, Zihan Liu, Ruyang Li, Hui Wei, Yaqian Zhao, Jingwen Leng, Minyi Guo, Yu Feng
abstract: This paper presents Atlas, an algorithm-hardware co-design system for on-device city-scale 3D Gaussian Splatting in mobile VR. The system employs hierarchical memory offloading and optimized rendering pipelines to achieve 18.5x speedup and 92.4% energy savings compared to baseline approaches, enabling city-scale 3D reconstruction directly on mobile VR hardware.

title: RACE-AIMC: Selective Inference for Heterogeneous Analog In-Memory Accelerators at the Edge
authors: Osama Yousuf, Martin Lueker-Boden
abstract: Analog in-memory computing (AIMC) speeds up neural-network inference by doing the arithmetic directly inside a memory array, instead of shuttling weights back and forth between memory and a processor. This saves energy, but physical devices that store the weights are imperfect. RACE-AIMC introduces a selective inference approach for heterogeneous analog in-memory accelerators at the edge, achieving certified inference with 69% energy reduction. The method handles device imperfections through selective routing of computations across heterogeneous AIMC units.

title: Hardware-Accelerated Instance Segmentation for Resource-Constrained Space Robotics
authors: Siddhant Shete, Hilmi Dogu Kucuker, Udo Frese, Frank Kirchner
abstract: This paper presents a quantized YOLO instance segmentation model deployed on a lunar micro-rover's DPU (Deep Processing Unit). Using activation variance sampling and criticality analysis, the system achieves reliable perception under radiation and low-light conditions with 309ms latency and 5.7W power consumption. The work demonstrates hardware-accelerated deep learning inference on radiation-tolerant edge hardware for space robotics applications.

title: Sustainable Edge Vision via Empirically Calibrated DVFS: Eliminating Thermal Throttling on Passively Cooled Hardware
authors: Aayush Marasini, Zhaoxian Zhou
abstract: Fanless cooling saves power but causes thermal throttling during continuous DNN inference on edge SoCs. The authors introduce a calibrated DVFS (Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling) scheduler using time guards and temperature limits to eliminate thermal throttling on passively cooled Raspberry Pi 5 running YOLOv8n, achieving 6.8% higher framerate compared to default governors while maintaining sustainable thermal operation.

title: Para-Pipe: Exploiting Hierarchical Operator Parallelism of ML Computational Graphs on SoCs
authors: Yujie Zhang, Huiying Lan, Ehsan Aghapour, Zhiyuan Ning, Peng Zan, Weidong Shao, Anuj Pathania, Tulika Mitra
abstract: As edge-based deep learning applications become more complex, optimizing performance on heterogeneous System-on-Chips (SoCs) presents unique challenges. Conventional pipelining effectively distributes computation across on-chip processing units for throughput, but fails to meet latency requirements of contemporary neural networks featuring complex interdependencies and extensive operator parallelism. Para-Pipe is a hierarchical mapping framework that integrates intra- and inter-stage operator parallelism within a pipelined architecture. Testing on Amlogic SoC (ARM big.LITTLE CPUs + GPU) and Black Sesame Technology SoC (DLA + DSPs) demonstrated 11.0% average energy efficiency improvement over purely pipelined strategies and 23.3% relative to non-pipelined parallel execution.

title: BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression via Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference
authors: Janghyeon Kim, Minsoo Kim, Kyuhong Shim, Jungwook Choi
abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) with extended chain-of-thought generation cause the KV cache to grow linearly with sequence length, creating critical memory bottlenecks. Current compression approaches rely on the assumption that recent queries reliably predict future attention, but this breaks down in long-horizon reasoning where certain decoding steps produce 'Thought Revisiting Tokens' that re-attend to distant prior context. BeaconKV introduces a training-free KV cache compression method that maintains compact representative 'beacon queries' as cluster representatives for each global similarity group, enabling the system to anticipate which KV pairs will be revisited without retaining the full query history. Tested across four open-source LRMs and multiple reasoning benchmarks, BeaconKV achieves up to 5.8x memory reduction and 4.3x throughput improvement while nearly preserving full cache accuracy. ICML 2026.

title: GrowPage: On-Demand KV Budgeting for Efficient LLM Reasoning Serving
authors: Qiankun Ma, Yanjiang Zhou, Zinan Xiong, Haofei Wang, Zhen Song, Yang Xiang, Ziyao Zhang, Hairong Zheng
abstract: Long-output reasoning makes the key-value (KV) cache a critical memory bottleneck for efficient LLM serving. Existing KV compression methods usually rely on a predefined per-request budget and ad-hoc static allocation during decoding. However, reasoning tasks show significant variability in memory needs across different prompts and throughout the generation process. GrowPage treats capacity dynamically as a flexible runtime asset, tracking short- and long-term attention patterns using lightweight two-timescale overviews. When limits are reached, the method either condenses existing states or allocates new memory pages, working alongside PagedAttention to maintain uninterrupted batch processing.

title: SGD-KV: Summarization Guided KV Cache Compression
authors: Zeyu Liu, Woomin Song, Xuandi Fu, Sai Muralidhar Jayanthi, Vivek Govindan, Aram Galstyan, Sravan Babu Bodapati, Srikanth Ronanki
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) face severe memory bottlenecks in long-context inference due to the linearly growing size of key-value (KV) caches. Existing KV cache compression techniques typically rely on importance scoring of individual KV entries, which can miss semantically important but low-attention tokens. SGD-KV introduces summarization-guided compression that uses summary tokens to identify which KV entries are critical for maintaining coherence and factual accuracy across long contexts.

title: FlexPosit: Tunable Fractional Precision for LLM Inference Accelerators
authors: Yimin Gao, Liangtao Dai, Jun Yin, Xinfei Guo, Mircea Stan
abstract: This paper addresses the compute and energy challenges of large language models through quantization. Finer granularity (e.g., group-wise) provides high accuracy but incurs scaling and control overhead, while coarser granularity (e.g., channel-wise) has lower overhead but loses accuracy at low precision. FlexPosit combines Posit-based quantization and a precision-tunable bit-serial architecture to bridge these gaps. The approach uses distribution-aware quantization with hardware-aligned, sensitivity-guided mixed-precision allocation to achieve group-wise accuracy with channel-wise regularity. Results show near-FP16 accuracy with sub-5-bit fractional weights, delivering up to 1.8x higher throughput and 2.0x lower energy than prior art. MICRO 2026.

title: Don't Drop Dropout: Optimizing Layer Sparsity for Efficient LLM Training and Inference
authors: Mostafa Elhoushi, Alex Pretko, Nolan Dey, Bin Claire Zhang, Gavia Gray, Gurpreet Gosal, Abdulrahman Mahmoud, Shane Bergsma, Joel Hestness
abstract: This paper demonstrates that layer dropout should be used in LLM training, showing up to 25% FLOPs savings during training and enabling post-training optimizations like early exit and self-speculative decoding with up to 1.5x speedup. The approach optimizes layer sparsity for both efficient training and inference.

title: Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion
authors: Subham Sekhar Sahoo, Lingjie Chen, Khiem Pham, Jonathan Geuter, Chaitanya Dwivedi, Varad Pimpalkhute, Yash Akhauri, Alexander Moreno, Mikhail Yurochkin, Zhenting Wang, Mostafa Elhoushi, Nolan Dey, Shane Bergsma, Joel Hestness, John Thickstun, Eric Xing, Zhengzhong Liu

Unlike speculative decoding which needs an auxiliary model, Uno integrates parallel token generation directly into the target model via discrete diffusion, eliminating draft-model overhead while maintaining output quality.

title: Compression Beyond the Uncompressed: DEX-Comp for RAG
authors: Shuyu Guo, Shuo Zhang, Zhaochun Ren
abstract: While providing AI with external information boosts capabilities, large context inputs reduce processing speed. DEX-Comp introduces a two-stage training recipe for soft context compression in RAG. In the first stage, the model learns from accurate answers of the uncompressed version. In the second stage, reinforcement learning is applied specifically to queries the larger model failed, compelling the compressed version to discover superior processing strategies. Experiments on five QA benchmarks (retrieval depths 5-30) demonstrate 16x context compression and 4-24x inference acceleration while matching or exceeding the uncompressed baseline.

title: Cache-Aware Joint Router Adaptation for Memory-Efficient MoE Inference
authors: Zhenhe Wu, Yaping Jin, Qinghua Xing, Hang Zhou, Wei He, Xianjie Wu, Xianfu Cheng, Jian Yang, Hanting Chen
abstract: In Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, the full expert set often exceeds GPU memory, causing repeated weight transfers during decoding. This paper treats expert-cache management as an algorithmic challenge and introduces a cache-aware post-training framework that jointly adapts the MoE backbone and lightweight auxiliary cache routers while maintaining standard Top-K expert selection. Two approaches are presented: a Temporal Router that predicts same-layer reuse and retains experts for future tokens, and a Spatio-Temporal Router that additionally uses predecessor hidden states to refine the cache. Testing on Qwen3 and GPT-OSS showed hit rate gains of 1.15-18.03 points and traffic reductions of 4.6-53.3%.

authors: Jundong Hu, Shekar Ramachandran
abstract: Removing complete transformer layers preserves a standard serving architecture, but existing depth-compression methods can lose substantial quality, and the loss varies unpredictably across models. XMerge introduces cross-axis selection and reconstructive layer merging for LLM depth compression, addressing the challenge of quality loss when removing transformer layers while maintaining standard serving infrastructure.

title: Debias-SparseGPT: Bias-Aware Pruning for Large Language Models
authors: Irina Proskurina, Guillaume Metzler, Antoine Gourru, Julien Velcin
abstract: Model compression techniques such as pruning and quantization facilitate the efficient deployment and acceleration of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, recent studies show that weight sparsification amplifies social biases in model outputs. Debias-SparseGPT introduces bias-aware pruning that simultaneously compresses models and reduces bias amplification, addressing the tension between deployment efficiency and fairness in LLM compression.

abstract: A free pause token gives a language model extra compute to form each next-token prediction (as a pause, or thinking token). title: Large Language Models with At Most One Spike per Neuron
authors: Zhuoya Zhao, Parsa Omidi, Aref Jafari, Richard Naud
abstract: This study investigates event-driven neural architectures as a low-power substitute for modern text generators. Limiting neuronal activation to a single event per window (TTFS coding) drastically reduces power consumption, but standard implementations fail to properly process essential mathematical operations and normalization steps. The authors developed a unique reference framework capable of processing embeddings, attention, and dropout layers. After training their custom architecture from scratch, they evaluated it on BERT and GPT-2 scale models. The system performed equally well as traditional networks on comprehension and logic evaluations, but struggled with perplexity scores. This marks the pioneer effort in growing this specific type of event-driven text model to 1.5 billion parameters, alongside offering theoretical power consumption estimates derived from activation counts.

title: A Reconfigurable Hybrid Convolutional-Fully Connected Neuromorphic Core for Biomedical Edge Inference

abstract: This study details a programmable FPGA setup for spiking convolutional neural network (SCNN) inference, applied to real-time hypoxia detection. The design uses a hybrid CNN-FC structure on quantized neuromorphic hardware, merging spatial-filtering and dense network tiers on specialized silicon. Initial evaluations utilizing standard image repositories yielded high correctness rates. When adapted for medical use with optical sensor readings and dermal pigmentation inputs, the model maintained strong correctness while using minimal electrical energy, proving its viability for portable health monitoring.

abstract: DNNs are widely applied in various industries. Specialized chips are being discussed for lower power consumption with higher throughput. Hardware variations introduced during chip manufacturing are the main cause of accuracy degradation on specialized DNN inference accelerator chips. This paper proposes hardware-conscious software training methods that recover accuracy degradation caused by manufacturing variabilities, enabling co-design of software training to compensate for hardware imperfections in production on-device inference.

abstract: H3DNAS presents a hardware-aware compression framework operating directly on ONNX graphs without requiring source code. title: Forgetting Without Restarting: Execution-State Unlearning for Stateful LLM Agents
authors: Chao Yao, Yangbo Wei, Zhen Huang, Junhong Qian, Chenle Chen, Shaoqiang Lu, Chen Wu, Lei He
abstract: Long-running LLM agents are stateful: beyond the transcript they accrete compressed summaries, plaintext memory, pending tool plans, and, under every serving API, a KV cache. Yet today's 'forget' operations are inadequate, deleting records while leaving every artifact derived from the revoked information intact. This paper formalizes execution-state unlearning, proving that exact unlearning requires at least T-tau+1 recomputed transitions. The proposed Provenance-Guided Selective Replay attains this bound as a cross-layer contract spanning prompt, compressed memory, and cache. Testing shows memory deletion leaves leakage unchanged and instruction-based forgetting collapses under elicitation, while the proposed approach achieves results indistinguishable from a full reset at up to 9x fewer recomputed tokens.

abstract: Biological agents navigate familiar environments not by re-solving routes for each new goal, but by reusing a learned map. This paper introduces compact Bellman-grounded cognitive maps that enable cost-aware navigation, allowing agents to efficiently plan paths by leveraging learned value functions rather than repeatedly solving optimal control problems.

authors: Vasileios Rizeakos, Georgios Paisios, Alexandros Machairas, Michael Birbas, Athanasios Bachoumis

title: ACE: Adaptive Calibration-Free Expert Skipping for Mixture-of-Experts
authors: Zukang Xu, Zhixiong Zhao, Xing Hu
abstract: ACE introduces a training-free, calibration-free expert skipping method for MoE models that achieves a 50% skip ratio with strong accuracy preservation. Unlike existing methods that require calibration data or additional training, ACE adaptively determines which experts to skip based on runtime signals alone, making it immediately applicable for deployment scenarios where calibration data is unavailable.
edge_agent_evidence: 免训练免校准MoE专家跳过，50%跳过率保持精度
recommendation_reason: 免校准MoE推理加速，对端侧MoE模型部署有直接价值

title: Substrate-Aware AI Agents: Execution Context as First-Class Input
authors: Manu Agrawal
abstract: This paper introduces substrate-aware AI agents that plan with memory, compute, and time constraints as first-class inputs. The system tests on 128MB RAM contracts, demonstrating that agents which explicitly reason about their execution substrate (available memory, compute budget, latency constraints) make better planning decisions than substrate-agnostic approaches. This directly addresses the challenge of deploying AI agents on resource-constrained devices.
edge_agent_evidence: 资源感知Agent(128MB RAM合约)，将执行约束作为一等输入
recommendation_reason: 直接面向资源受限设备的Agent规划，将硬件约束纳入Agent决策

title: Hardware-Aware FP4 FlashAttention-4
authors: Robert Hu
abstract: This paper addresses limitations of Blackwell's 4-bit floating-point (FP4) tensor cores which do not automatically make attention faster because softmax conversion and on-chip dependencies dominate once matrix products shrink. The author introduces Direct-P for noncausal inference and a causal path that passes forward quantization directly into backward. Direct-P maps scores directly to FP4 probabilities and reaches up to 2.13x the bfloat16 forward throughput on an NVIDIA GB200. For causal training, it reconstructs probabilities from saved quantized queries and keys using FP8 gradient operands, accelerating a complete single-GPU 8B parameter update by up to 1.14x.
edge_agent_evidence: FP4 FlashAttention-4在GB200上达2.13x BF16吞吐，硬件感知注意力
recommendation_reason: FP4注意力优化，新一代硬件上的高效推理核心技术

title: From Deep to Shallow: Unconstrained Layer Merging Strategy
authors: Petro Shulzhenko, Gabriele Spadaro, Enzo Tartaglione
abstract: This paper introduces an unconstrained layer merging strategy for depth compression that is validated on real embedded platforms. The approach enables merging convolutional layers with padding, a capability that previous depth-compression methods lacked. By removing the constraint of only merging identical layers, the method achieves more aggressive depth reduction while maintaining model quality on resource-constrained hardware.
edge_agent_evidence: 无约束层合并深度压缩，在真实嵌入式平台上验证
recommendation_reason: 嵌入式平台验证的层合并压缩方法，直接减少推理深度

title: When Quantization Breaks Memory: Recurrent-State Write-Back
authors: Ismail Erbas, Xavier Intes, Vikas Pandey
abstract: This paper reveals that quantized recurrent state write-back causes accuracy collapse from 0.94 to 0.39 in temporal inference tasks. When quantized hidden states are written back to the model's recurrent memory and then read in subsequent steps, quantization errors compound catastrophically. This finding is critical for deploying quantized models in any setting with persistent state (RNNs, SSMs, or agents with memory), particularly on edge devices where quantization is essential for fitting models in limited memory.
edge_agent_evidence: 量化导致循环状态写回精度崩塌(0.94→0.39)，对端侧量化部署有关键警示
recommendation_reason: 揭示量化在循环推理中的精度崩塌问题，对端侧量化部署有重要警示意义

title: Compact-Memory LLM Agents via Online Max-Member Clustering
authors: Jiahe Geng, Jinpeng Wang, Kun Yuan
abstract: This paper introduces compact-memory LLM agents that use online max-member clustering to maintain 83% of full-context quality at only 32% of the token cost. Operating in the 2k-5k prompt budget regime, the approach dynamically clusters and compresses agent memory while preserving critical information. This enables long-running agents to operate within tight memory constraints typical of on-device deployment.
edge_agent_evidence: 紧凑型Agent内存，32% token开销保持83%全上下文质量，2k-5k预算
recommendation_reason: Agent内存压缩方法，使端侧Agent在严格token预算下运行

title: On-board ML for Trace Gas Detection in Imaging Spectroscopy
authors: Vit Ruzicka, Adam Chlus, Andrew Thorpe
abstract: This paper demonstrates on-board (satellite/airborne) machine learning inference for real-time trace gas detection in imaging spectroscopy. The system replaces ground-processing pipelines with direct on-board inference, enabling immediate detection of gas emissions without the latency of downlinking raw hyperspectral data. This represents a practical deployment of ML inference on resource-constrained spaceborne platforms.
edge_agent_evidence: 星载/机载平台上实时ML推理，替代地面处理管线
recommendation_reason: 资源受限星载平台的ML推理部署实例

title: Distilled Continuous Diffusion LMs: Code in Few Steps or One
authors: Fred Zhangzhi Peng, Kaiwen Zheng, Anru Zhang
abstract: This paper introduces distilled continuous diffusion language models that can generate code in few steps or even a single step. By distilling the iterative denoising process of diffusion language models, the approach dramatically reduces the sequential token generation bottleneck. Single-step or few-step generation is particularly valuable for on-device inference where iterative refinement is computationally expensive.
edge_agent_evidence: 蒸馏连续扩散语言模型实现少步/单步代码生成
recommendation_reason: 少步/单步生成减少推理迭代开销，对端侧部署有直接价值

title: ElderBench: Benchmarking Autonomous Mobile Agents for Older Adults
authors: Weide Zhan, Qumu Shaqu, Yuanqing Liu
abstract: ElderBench is a dedicated benchmark for evaluating autonomous mobile agents that assist older adults with smartphone tasks. The benchmark evaluates GUI-based mobile interaction capabilities including app navigation, form filling, and multi-step task completion in scenarios relevant to elderly users. It provides standardized evaluation for the emerging category of mobile phone assistance agents.
edge_agent_evidence: 面向老年人智能手机辅助的自主移动Agent评测基准
recommendation_reason: 移动端Agent评测基准，评估手机上的自主Agent能力

title: Communication-Efficient Personalized Federated Learning
authors: Xu Zhang, Xingyu Hou, Jiacheng Cheng
abstract: This paper introduces layer-wise quantization for communication-efficient personalized federated learning on distributed edge devices. The approach balances model personalization with communication cost by selectively quantizing different model layers based on their sensitivity to precision reduction, enabling practical federated training on bandwidth-constrained edge networks.
edge_agent_evidence: 层级量化通信高效联邦学习，面向带宽受限边缘网络
recommendation_reason: 端侧联邦学习的通信效率优化方法

title: LookThere! Sparse Vision by Reinforced Selection
authors: Sreehari Rammohan, Yousef Yassin, Anthony Fuller
abstract: LookThere introduces RL-trained input selection for efficient vision that processes only 0.2% of input pixels while maintaining accuracy. The reinforced selection mechanism learns which regions of an image are most informative, dramatically reducing the computational cost of visual processing. This sparse vision approach is particularly valuable for edge devices where processing full-resolution images is prohibitive.
edge_agent_evidence: 仅处理0.2%像素的稀疏视觉，RL训练输入选择器
recommendation_reason: 极端稀疏视觉方法(0.2%输入)，对端侧视觉处理有重要价值
